cards.front: Someone asks you to move funds or sign something
cards.back: Verify through a second channel (call or a known handle) before doing anything.
Don't click. Report it in #security-alerts within one hour.
Hardware security key (2FA) on every account, no SMS codes.
Report to IT Security within one hour, even at 3 a.m.
Blackout: no LDO trades 14 days before and after a vote you worked on.

cards.front: Advising or investing in another staking protocol
cards.back: Disclose it to People Ops before you start. Disclosure ≠ ban.
Up to $100 is fine. Above that, disclose it to People Ops.
Only Comms speaks for Lido. Personal posts say "my own views".
Approved tools only. No contributor data or unreleased code in personal accounts.
Async first: write it down in a doc, then meet only if needed.
Agenda in the invite, 45 minutes max, notes shared after.
14:00–17:00 UTC: be reachable for calls and quick replies.
25 days a year. Post in your team channel at least 2 weeks ahead.
Tell your lead the same morning and rest. No sick-day cap.
Once a year. Receipts uploaded within 30 days.
Economy for flights under 6 hours; book 3+ weeks ahead.
Every newcomer gets a buddy for the first 30 days. Ask them anything.
The decentralised organisation that governs the Lido protocol.
Vote on upgrades, treasury spending and annual goals of the DAO.
Lets stETH holders delay or block DAO decisions they disagree with.
The public forum where proposals are discussed before any vote.
Off-chain signalling vote: checks the DAO's sentiment.
The binding vote that actually executes a change.
Fast lane for routine motions: passes unless enough LDO objects.
Builds and maintains the protocol code, upgrades and new features.
Grows the ecosystem around Lido: products, integrations, adoption.
Supports partner protocols aligned with Ethereum and Lido.
The DAO's goal framework: three-year objectives and yearly goals.
Yearly grant requests that fund the foundations' work toward GOOSE.
Lido Ecosystem Grants Organisation: gives grants to builders.
Professional and community teams that run Lido's validators.
Locking ETH to help secure Ethereum and earn rewards.
Staking where you get a token back, so your ETH stays usable.
The token you get for staking ETH with Lido; its balance grows daily.
Wrapped stETH: fixed balance, value grows. Easier for DeFi apps.
A machine with 32 ETH that proposes and checks Ethereum blocks.
The daily update that adds staking rewards to stETH balances.
Where stETH waits to be turned back into ETH.
A penalty that burns part of a validator's ETH for breaking rules.
Yearly reward rate, shown without compounding.
An organisation run by token votes instead of a board of directors.
Financial apps on blockchains: lending, trading, without banks.
The DAO's own funds, spent only by tokenholder decision.
Outside security experts review code before it goes live.
A wallet that needs several signers to approve a transaction.
The fee paid to Ethereum to process a transaction.

scenarios.situation: A "core dev" DMs you on Telegram asking for your wallet seed phrase to "fix a bug".
scenarios.explain: Nobody ever needs your seed phrase. Report it in #security-alerts.

scenarios.situation: Your lead emails at night: "urgent, pay this vendor invoice now, no time to call".
scenarios.explain: Verify through a second channel before moving any funds.

scenarios.situation: You paste a screenshot of the multisig signing screen with a recovery phrase visible into a Slack thread.
scenarios.explain: Keys and phrases never go into chats or screenshots.

scenarios.situation: You get a DM with a link to "claim your contributor airdrop". You report it in #security-alerts and don't click.
scenarios.explain: Exactly right: don't click, report within an hour.

scenarios.situation: Setting up your new work account, you choose SMS codes because the security key is in another room.
scenarios.explain: Hardware key on every account, no SMS.

scenarios.situation: Your laptop is stolen on Saturday night. You plan to tell IT on Monday.
scenarios.explain: Report within one hour, any day, any time.

scenarios.situation: You helped draft a governance proposal. Vote is next week. You want to buy some LDO today.
scenarios.explain: Trading blackout: 14 days before and after votes you worked on.

scenarios.situation: A friend's staking startup asks you to be an advisor. You tell People Ops first.
scenarios.explain: Disclose before you start. Disclosure isn't a ban.

scenarios.situation: A partner sends you a $400 watch after a conference.
scenarios.explain: Over $100: disclose it to People Ops.

scenarios.situation: You tweet: "Lido is launching X next month!" from your personal account.
scenarios.explain: Only Comms speaks for Lido, and unreleased plans stay private.

scenarios.situation: You paste unreleased contract code into your personal AI chat to debug it.
scenarios.explain: Approved AI tools only, never with unreleased code.

scenarios.situation: Before scheduling a call, you write a one-page doc with options and ask for comments.
You book a 90-minute call with no agenda "to brainstorm".
scenarios.explain: Agenda in the invite, 45 minutes max.

scenarios.situation: You post your two-week vacation in the team channel a month ahead.
scenarios.explain: Sunbed Days: 2+ weeks notice, you're well ahead.

scenarios.situation: You wake up with a fever and message your lead that you're off today.
scenarios.explain: Tell your lead the same morning and rest.

scenarios.situation: You bought a monitor with your allowance 3 months ago and still haven't uploaded the receipt.
You book business class for a 2-hour flight to a conference.
Week two, you're not sure who owns the expense tool. You ask your Goose Buddy.
